# DANI DECLARES — Business Build & Commercialization Agreement

**DRAFT / ATTORNEY REVIEW REQUIRED BEFORE SIGNATURE**

## Purpose
DANI DECLARES LLC (“DANI”) provides business-building, commercialization, operational infrastructure, and scaling support to a client (“Client”). The parties may also authorize Client to participate in the DANI Capability Network under a separate or incorporated Network Access Schedule.

## 1. Scope
The selected package/order form controls the exact deliverables. Services may include business/service architecture, offer design, pricing support, packaging, branding/marketing implementation, website/intake/payment setup, administrative systems, SOP/workflow development, customer acquisition support, operational scaling, and network-readiness.

## 2. Commercial Authority
Only the authority expressly granted in the signed agreement applies. Where granted, DANI may establish or manage commercial presentation, pricing, marketing, intake, customer workflow, and operational systems for the Client’s DANI-supported offering. Authority does not transfer ownership of the Client’s legal entity unless expressly stated.

## 3. Network Access
If included in the selected package or agreement, DANI may enable Network Access. Network Access permits the Client to view and accept eligible DANI opportunities only after applicable identity, capability, credential, insurance, agreement, and SKU-authorization requirements are satisfied. Network Access is not employment and does not guarantee work, revenue, minimum bookings, or income.

## 4. Compensation
The applicable order form must state one compensation model: upfront fee, installment/monthly fee, project fee, deferred fee, milestone fee, revenue-based fee, or a permitted combination. For deferred or revenue-based arrangements, the agreement must define the triggering event, revenue/payment definition, reporting method, calculation, payment deadline, audit/reporting rights, expenses, term, and post-termination treatment.

## 5. Expenses
No material third-party expense is reimbursable unless approved under the order form or written change authorization.

## 6. Client Responsibilities
Client remains responsible for the truthfulness of information supplied to DANI, legal/licensing requirements applicable to Client’s profession, performance of the underlying professional service, and obligations of Client’s own business unless expressly delegated in writing.

## 7. Intellectual Property
The order form must identify pre-existing IP, DANI-owned work product, Client-owned work product, licenses, reusable templates, trademarks, domain names, account credentials, and post-termination access.

## 8. Network Provider Status
If Client also fulfills DANI work, Client’s provider relationship is governed by the applicable Provider Agreement and Service Schedule. Business-build status does not itself authorize any service.

## 9. Compliance
No regulated service may be marketed or assigned without required licensing, credentialing, insurance, and jurisdictional verification. DANI may suspend an offering or network access when compliance information expires or becomes insufficient.

## 10. Confidentiality / Data Security
The parties will protect confidential business, customer, financial, and operational information. Access to financial or customer systems is limited to the minimum necessary for the authorized scope.

## 11. Term / Termination
The order form controls the term. Termination provisions must address unfinished work, accrued/deferred compensation, active customer commitments, network access, intellectual property, data return, and post-termination payment obligations.

## 12. No Guaranteed Results
DANI does not guarantee revenue, funding, customer acquisition, profitability, rankings, approvals, or network work unless a specific written performance obligation expressly says otherwise.

## 13. Legal Review
This draft is an operational starting point and must be reviewed and customized by qualified counsel for the actual relationship, jurisdiction, compensation model, tax treatment, worker classification, intellectual property, and regulated-industry issues before execution.
